The middle nodes C and D have the minimum eccentricity 2 and are drawn in the accent color. The card returns their node ids, 3 and 4." width="100%"} The eccentricity of a node is the largest hop distance from it to any node it can reach. Center nodes have the smallest eccentricity, equal to the graph's radius, so from them every other node is as near as possible in the worst case. This is the classic answer to "where should a single facility go so that nobody is too far away" (the minimax location), and the counterpart of `get_periphery()`. Distances are computed by breadth-first search, so edge weights are ignored, as in `eccentricity()` and `get_periphery()`. The candidates are the same as in `get_radius()`: only nodes that reach every node of their (weakly) connected component, skipping single-node components unless the graph has no edges between distinct nodes. So an isolated node, or a sink in a directed graph, is never central just because it reaches nothing. On a disconnected graph the center comes from the component(s) with the smallest radius. For the node minimizing the *total* distance instead, see `get_barycenter()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted IDs of the center nodes. Empty for an empty graph, or a directed graph where no node reaches its whole component. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The middle of a path is its center; a path with an even number of nodes has two: ::: {#402d066a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5).get_center(), ec.Graph().add_path_graph(6).get_center() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([3], [3, 4]) ``` ::: ::: The center is pulled toward long branches: here the chain D-E-F-G moves it off the hub A and onto D and E: ::: {#a5ccbd3c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "G")]) ) [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in graph.get_center()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['D', 'E'] ``` ::: :::
